speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you have experienced occasional shooting ear pain and difficulty wearing earrings following a tympanoplasty; to help me identify the complication, can you describe exactly where the pain is located and what specific symptoms you notice when attempting to wear earrings?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Recurrent Granulation Tissue (Surgical Granulation) in the Right Ear Canal.

The history of pain while eating suggests possible myringosclerosis or Eustachian tube dysfunction, while the specific discomfort with earrings indicates a mass effect or tenderness in the ear canal consistent with granulation tissue forming at the tympanoplasty site. I will proceed with this diagnosis based on the clinical presentation and risk factors provided.
